heading: India vs Japan Highlights, Asian Games T20: IND seal semifinal spot in 5 overs
paragraphs: Questions may persist about the transition and a wobbly middle order, but the bid for a gold medal in Aichi-Nagoya will take priority for now. And Harmanpreet Kaur’s team has begun in rampant fashion, crushing hosts Japan in their Asian Games quarter-final in Nisshin on Friday.

Bowling first, the Asia Cup winners were too hot for the fledgling Japanese side. While they managed to hold fort, the hosts rarely posed any threat and stretched the innings for as long as they could, eventually mustering 57 runs in 19.5 overs.

The chase was cleaned up in manic fashion, albeit accounting for the early dismissals of G Kamalini and Bharti Fulmali. Led by a belligerent Shafali Verma, India closed the chase in only five overs in their first-ever T20I meeting against Japan.

Kato sprays the ball on length and Shafali creams it through cover for FOUR. Another loosener outside off-stump and Shafali slashes hard through point for FOUR more. In the slot this time and Richa muscles the ball past wide long-on for another FOUR. 50 up, can India close the chase in this over? Low full-toss and Richa taps it to the deep for a single. India are one hit away. And Shafali Ghosh smites the ball over long-on for a huge six, sealing the chase and India's semi-final spot in 5 overs!

Another wicket for Japan! Ayaka Kato-Stafford strikes with her fourth delivery as Fulmali fluffs a slog across the line. The ball bites the outside edge and lobs up straight to the point fielder and India have lost two in quick succession. And despite that, Shafali isn't one to hold back as she deposits her second delivery over long-off for SIX!
Bharti Fulmali c Kato b Kato-Stafford 6 (7b 1x4)

First wicket for Japan! Kamalini steps out and hacks a delivery sliding towards the pads and finds the long-on fielder. A well judged catch in the deep and Japan have inflicted an unlikely dismissal. Bharti Fulmali is in at 3.
Gunalan Kamalini c Chandel b Nonoha Yasumoto 0 (2b)
No Mandhana! Shafali Verma and G Kamalini walk out to open India's chase. Left-arm pacer Chandel to begin proceedings.

A loosener outside the off-stump and Shafali flays the first ball through extra cover for FOUR. A wide follows down leg and Chandel moves into the slot once again. Shafali punishes the length with another biff down the ground for FOUR. Wide outside the off-stump this time and Shafali merely hangs his bat away from the body and cashes in another FOUR! Much better this time as Chandel attacks the stumps from length, forcing Shafali to tap back at her. Width, and punished again, Shafali nails another delivery straying on length through extra cover, closing the over with her fourth FOUR of the over. And India are nearly a third through the chase already.

Smriti Mandhana and Shreyanka Patil cannot stifle a few chuckles as the ball trickles off to knock a bail down off Yasumoto's bat. Even the Japanese batters cannot hide a few laughs, seemingly enjoying the occasion to the fullest as the innings closes at 19.5 overs with 57 runs on the board. Must be a walk in the park for India before officially locking in on their semi-final berth against Bangladesh over the next 30 minutes.

No. 3 for Sree Charani. Nishimura top-edges a loopy delivery from length and a simple catch lands in the hands of Fulmali at short mid-wicket. Another one bites the dust. Action replay from two deliveries back as Sree Charani finds another miscue off length. Toguchi sends the ball straight up and Shafali pouches a simple catch from a few yards behind the umpire.
Double-wicket maiden for Sree Charani as she bowls out with figures of 4-2-10-4.
Akari Nishimura c Fulmali b Shree Charani 2 (9b); Erika Toguchi-Quinn c Shafali Verma b Shree Charani 0 (2b)

Shafali returns for the 17th over and her third delivery was a half-tracker around off, Kato tries to get it over mid-off and ends up holing out right there. Then Mandhana with a quick throw from fine leg and Ghosh flicks the bail to run out Hinase Goto as the Japanese tried to pinch a second run.
That's the end of Kato-Stafford's stay in the middle. She takes a big swing at the second ball of the 15th by Shafali, which was full and on off. Ends up holing out at mid-on.
Deepti's last ball in the 12th over is sent in full outside off. Erika Oda hits it leg side and Shreyanka takes an easy catch at deep midwicket.

Shafali Verma rolled her arms over for this one, she is a wicket-taker but no poles for her in this over. A couple of runs for the Japanese. Their opener Ayaka Kato-Stafford is still out there. She has played for the Australian U19 team and well, she might still be eligible to play for that side based on her age alone - Kato-Stafford is just 16 years old.
Deepti bowled the 10th over of the Japanese innings. A couple of singles squeezed through, with the first of those probably one that India should have prevented.

There was no hat-trick for Charani, with Erika Oda blocking out the fourth delivery and the rest of the over as well. Well, even those who don't know much about cricket would probably know that India are the heavy favourites to win today and thus far, the gap is quite visible out in the middle.
One brings two! Mai Yanagida the captain ends up nicking it behing and Richa Ghosh makes no mistake with the catch. Shree Charani on a hat-trick.

GONE! Haruna Iwasaki goes down on one knee, trying to slog Charani's second ball of the seventh over down the ground for a big one. She ends up hitting it straight down the throat of Shafali Verma at long-on.
Iwasaki c Shafali Verma b Shree Charani 10 (22)

Shreyanka Patil, back in the side after a long spell on the sidelines due to injury, bowled the last over of the powerplay. She sent the third ball wide down the leg side and then Kato-Stafford took a single off the next ball. Another single came off the last ball.

Shree Charani comes into the attack, her third delivery was full and tossed up outside off. Kano swings, it takes a thick outside edge and beats slip to go to the boundary for Japan's first four of these Games. Kano gets off strike next ball and then Iwasaki sends the last ball over mid-on for another four.

Nandani continues to sling the ball down towards middle-and-leg, and Iwasaki nudges another one across the square for a single. No change in intent yet, as the Japanese openers continue to tap the deliveries along the ground. Change of pace from Nandani and the batters sneak in couple of runs off overthrows from Richa Ghosh down the ground, towards the sightscreen. In the slot and the first aerial stroke from Japan as Iwasaki lifts Nandana down the ground for two runs.

Nishimura and Iwasaki hold fort but that wouldn't be enough in the long run this morning. Just the two runs have trickled per over so far as the Indian pacers have held their line firmly along the stumps. JAP-W 6/0 in 3 overs

Length ball attacking the stumps and Nishimura opens her account with a flick across the line for a single. A string of dots and a wide follows. A consistent attack on the wickets, but the Japanese openers are just about managing to hold the ball off the stumps.
Kranti Gaud to open proceedings with the ball.

Gaud rushes a couple of deliveries past Iwasaki's blade and the right-hander gets bat on ball for the first time from the third. A gentle push through the covers and Japan gain their first couple of runs in the contest. Gaud continues to pummel the length hard, rushing past the outside edge. JAP-W 2/0 in 1 over
The teams line up for the national anthems. This will be the first-ever international featuring India and Japan at the senior level.

Vinay Iyer, a Mumbai club cricketer who once arranged his life around a 5.15am bus to make practice on time, will be on the other side of the boundary rope on Friday, as coach of Japan’s women’s cricket team at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Their opponents: India. READ MORE from Mihir Vasavda

Questions linger over Harmanpreet's contributions as a batter in the current order, along with her future as the leader of a side that also boasts of Smriti Mandhana. None of it, though, stopped India from reclaiming the Asia Cup throne in Dubai last week, with Shafali Verma and Mandhana taking centre stage against Sri Lanka. READ MORE

The makeshift Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin will not be the only major cricket venue in Japan over the course of the next few days. Owing to a special occasion on September 22, the Indian men's cricket team will also gear up for a special one-off T20I against Japan at the Sano International Cricket Ground, about 100 kilometres from Tokyo. The first cricket quarter-final was washed out in Nisshin on Thursday, with Bangladesh proceeding to the semis without a ball being bowled.
India not a sporting superpower, but can make presence felt at Asian Games
India has won 778 medals at Asian Games till date from 19 editions – 183 of them being gold. China has 3,570 in all, with 1,674 gold; that too from 14 outings.

Those numbers – and a small, unassuming knick-knack tucked inside the goodie-bag given to every Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games athlete – can put the next fortnight into perspective.
